# Events, queues, and asynchronous processing

- Authenticate services and authorize publish/subscribe access per topic, queue, tenant, and environment. Do not rely on an internal network as the trust boundary.
- Treat message headers, keys, payloads, schemas, and replayed historical events as untrusted. Validate a versioned schema and semantic limits before processing.
- Use data-only serialization. Do not deserialize arbitrary language objects, class names, expressions, or externally resolved schemas.
- Include a stable event type/version and immutable identifiers. Validate tenant and actor context against authoritative data rather than trusting claims in the message.
- Design consumers for at-least-once delivery: make side effects idempotent, bind deduplication to the operation/tenant, and commit acknowledgement only after the intended durable outcome.
- Make state transitions atomic with the event/outbox/inbox record where consistency matters. Avoid check-then-act races and unbounded redelivery loops.
- Bound message size, batch size, concurrency, processing time, retries, backoff, and dead-letter retention. Treat poison messages without blocking an entire partition indefinitely.
- Protect sensitive data in transit and at rest; minimize payloads and keep credentials/tokens out of events, error queues, traces, and broker management UI.
- Verify integrity/authenticity end-to-end when broker ACLs do not cover the threat model. Rotate signing/encryption keys without accepting downgrade or cross-environment replay.
- Audit privileged commands and operational replays. Reauthorization may be required when delayed processing occurs after a user's permissions or object state has changed.
